turns.content: A real, stationary, spherically symmetric wavefunction is confined to d1<r<100d1. Measurements give the same probability P in the adjacent shells d1<r<2d1 and 2d1<r<3d1, even though the second shell has greater volume. What does this say about the shells' average probability per unit volume?
Does that comparison by itself show that moving a particle outward causes its local probability density to decrease, or does it establish only an association within this stationary state?
What quantum-mechanical radial measure, including the spherical volume factor, should be used to compare probabilities in the two shells?
For a real spherically symmetric wavefunction psi(r), write the probability of finding the particle between arbitrary radii a and b.
Within the candidate power-law family psi(r)=C r^n, express the radial probability integrand in terms of n.
Find the exponent n for which adjacent shells of equal radial width have equal probability, and justify why no other power-law exponent has that property here.
Which candidate radial dependence for psi(r) follows from that exponent and the two equal shell probabilities?
Is this wavefunction normalizable on d1<r<100d1, and why does the positive inner radius remove the apparent divergence at r=0?
Verify the result by evaluating the two shell integrals up to their common constant, and keep the observational conclusion separate from any causal claim about radius.
State the final radial form of the wavefunction and the appropriate observational qualification.
